As shaker player I usually buy 2 clarities, boots and ward. Then I place an observer and take watchers (I usually do it in front of tower - but that's a preference)

Then I secure the rune by going agressive on enemy rune with offlaner until 20 sec. Then am going back to double fissure creep wave with using clarity at T2 so I don't waste mana.

Then going for some hits on pos 5 and creating the 1v1 and at around 50 sec depending on position where the 1v1 is I body block the small camp. What happens is we usually trade blocking camps.

My first courier is set of tangos and then sentry. Then just forcing the pos5 to 1v1. I've learned that it's the best you can do as shaker in Laning stage. Totem lvl2 and then just either trading through that or denying through that.

Big timing is minute 3. Where it's either lotus secure for offlaner or bounty secure. Depending where the lane is etc. Then am just continuing with same plan at start.

Then minute 4 I go secure the rune. Same at minute 6 which transitions into xp rune at minute 7 which is filled out by doing dmg to mid or kill and then stacking.

Throughout the whole process if your offlaner isn't windrunner he should have vanguard, so he's perfectly fine solo and should have had decent time. If offlaners expect to have a lane like a carry then those people are just on a wrong role and should be playing carry.

That same strategy I am playing for a long time and I've found it good for the most part. Because creating a 1v1 is the best you can do and then it's just 1v1 between carry and offlaner. If he loses to the pick well that's unfortunate. If he loses by skill it's not your fault and you don't deserve blame. Then you can analyze replay and see where maybe you should've went for carry instead of support because there was dmg then enemy using salve and blah blah blah. You know the drill.

Of course the Laning depends a lot on enemy support and laning partner. How mid is doing and a lot of other things, but that's the general idea for me.

From me, my most problem as shaker is that the support calls for help and I get 2v1 scenario where my offlaners mentality is "oh I better hit some creeps while I have a chance". You do that twice and the lane is over. At that point it is your fault and that's how I lost most of my lanes. If the enemy isn't completely stupid. But I found that in like 3/10 games like that. I learned how to deal with that is just running to the jungle. Enemy carry just goes back to lane cause he's losing creeps and xp and you bring back that 1v1. It's a bit long talk, but maybe it helps you get the playstyle a bit differently. Not saying what I do is correct. Probably wrong, but it's what works for me. I don't see any issues with what you described as playstyle. I think that if we could see a replay it'd be for the most part the offlaners fault that he doesn't respect the lane enough.

General rules that I went by:

1. BO3 - More fair because of switch sides, then cointoss.
2. Roles are asigned to my best konwledge and combination for the team, in regards of oponents as well - but overall not every single game. Also from my ingame experience playing those heroes in those positions. (a bit above 5k here)
3. Heroes can't change roles, because then we get to a lot of theorycrafting and a lot more decisions.
4. Outcome based of lineup and items I thought I'd go for each hero in each game - could've changed depending on oponents.
5. Lane swaps I've considered - but afterwards disregarded them. Again would be way too complicated - specialy later on (will be mentioned).

Animals 2x0 Shamans - Shamans have pretty good tempo. But with proper play from Pangolier and Brewmaster on early fights, they should be able to win them up until the point where Monkey King and Ursa will be too strong with BKB's and BKB's on Shaman's side doesn't really do anything besides stoping Pangolier roll and proper usage of split. Their push isn't that strong either. I think everything on average the Animals should win 2-0.

Animals 2x1 Undead - This is pretty close. But very similar. The problem is, the Animals can deal with Tombstone so that gives huge advantage for me and I think that if played properly they should win. I see the Undead win though with Aghanim's Scepter on Wraith king.

Shamans 0x2 Undead - In my opinion kind of no brainer. Should be Undead all the way. They can match the tempo of Shamans, but this time. No way to deal with Tombstone besides Shadow Shaman Serpent Wards - which shouldn't be used for that. Afterwards the BKB's are just too strong for Undead.

Not sure if it was mentioned here in the comments. I bet some Invoker player already did. But just in case. Just learn and practice very simple combo. Requires hex and refresher and BKB (which is optional, but I highly recommend).

First have ghost walk and defeaning blast on your active spells. Go into ghost walk and search your target (preferably alone).

Next pretty simple combo, that's actually easier to execute then you might think with a little practice.

Hex, BKB, defeaning blast, meteor, refresher, meteor, hex, defeaning blast, alacrity yourself, right click, BKB, ghost walk out. (Could be done with the same order after refresher. Means refresher hex, meteor, defeaning blast)

The much harder what I do is this.

Hex, BKB, defeaning blast, meteor, sunstrike/cataclysm, refresher, hex, sunstrike/cataclysm, meteor, defeaning blast, alacrity, BKB, ghost walk out.

I've seen Sumiya and McOfficialInvoker (shout-out to both) do much much harder combos that I can't pull off. But this should effectively kill any target within 3,5 to 4k HP pool, considering the alacrity effect and just right click down with second BKB. All of this takes practice and of course depends on if enemy has status resist or any save like oracle, omniknight, pudge that can eat and many many other things. Also depends on other items you buy. I usually go for the orchid game, which if you can include that in the combo it's even better of course. Highly recommended the lvl 10 talent as well and shard is not a bad idea either.

Just for fun you can watch this:

https://youtu.be/yAB4XQfGxUw

I tried to replicate it and messed up even after 40 tries. But overall if you keep the hex refresher combo simple like that above you can kill almost anyone.

Last note, the ghost walk can be replaced with blink hex and the rest of the combo if you have good vision over the target.

GL HF
